intent: Overlap several Avatars into one stack, optionally capped by a count of the ones left out.
typical_uses: The participants of a thread, a call or a shared document shown as one stack

dont_use_when.situation: People who each need their name or an action shown beside their picture

invariants.text: The group lays its children out in a row and pulls every child after the first back by `var(--space-2)` so the circles overlap; later children paint over earlier ones, so the last in the markup sits on top.
Every Avatar that is a direct child of the group gets a 2px ring in the page background color, drawn outside its circle, so overlapping circles read as separate discs whatever each is filled with.
The group takes no size of its own and imposes none: each Avatar keeps its own `size`.

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap each Avatar in another element inside the group
anti_patterns.do_instead: Place the Avatars as direct children - the member ring and the count's size rule select only direct Avatar children of the group

rtl.by: avatar.module.css overlaps with a physical margin-left, so an RTL row does not overlap the way the invariant states

good.title: A stack of participants with a count of the rest
good.code:
<AvatarGroup>
  <Avatar>
    <AvatarImage src="/jane.jpg" alt="Jane Doe" />
    <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
  </Avatar>
  <Avatar>
    <AvatarImage src="/sam.jpg" alt="Sam Lee" />
    <AvatarFallback>SL</AvatarFallback>
  </Avatar>
  <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
</AvatarGroup>

bad.title: Avatars wrapped in extra elements inside the group
bad.why: The wrappers still overlap, but the Avatars inside them are no longer direct children of the group, so they lose the background ring that separates overlapping circles.
